metadata.case_name: LEUNG BON KAU v. LAU KONG

injuries.description: the posterior cruciate ligament, lateral ligaments complex and attenuated anterior cruciate ligament of the left knee were torn. These were all repaired.
source: the posterior cruciate ligament, lateral ligaments complex and attenuated anterior cruciate ligament of the left knee were torn. These were all repaired.
injuries.icd_description: Injury to multiple structures of knee

injuries.description: 5% permanent impairment for the cosmetic impairment psychologically and another 5% for the mild depressive reaction to the physical disabilities as directly caused by the accident.
source: She assessed the Plaintiff to be suffering from 5% permanent impairment for the cosmetic impairment psychologically and another 5% for the mild depressive reaction to the physical disabilities as directly caused by the accident.

manifestations.description: In October 1988 the range of movement was 20 - 60 degrees and the Plaintiff was able to walk with a walking stick.
he was not able to walk even one to two steps without the assistance of a walking stick unless he was holding onto something.
The disability on his left knee also disturbed his sleep.
I accept that he still suffers from residual pain and stiffness of the knee with post-traumatic degeneration.
I am satisfied that the Plaintiff did walk with a limp and did need a walking stick though he has grossly exaggerated his disability.
mild depressive reaction to the physical disabilities as directly caused by the accident (assessed at 5% permanent impairment).

treatments_received: surgical repair of torn posterior cruciate ligament, lateral ligament complex and attenuated anterior cruciate ligament
re-admissions for limitation of knee movements
treatments_future: possible knee fusion surgery (less than 50% chance)

losses.description: Residual pain and stiffness of the knee with post-traumatic degeneration; limitation of knee movement; needs a walking stick; walks with a limp; cannot walk long distances; disturbed sleep.
